subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw solve #41484 as a narrow per-job/heartbeat elevated flag, or fold elevated-exec approval into the broader non-forgeable scheduling and heartbeat provenance design?
rationale: The choice changes the trust boundary for host-elevated exec across persisted cron jobs, agent-created schedules, HEARTBEAT.md/config edits, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent model.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Treat #41484 as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design while explicitly keeping heartbeat provenance in scope.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat-modifier elevated approval state now, with explicit migration and tests for create, update, and execution-time checks.

options.title: Remove Internal-Source Elevation
options.body: Fail closed for cron-event and heartbeat elevated access unless maintainers intentionally preserve a compatibility path.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Treat #41484 as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design while explicitly keeping heartbeat provenance in scope.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged cron caller-scope work makes joshavant the closest current owner path for scheduling provenance decisions.
